jobs.description:
At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.

Position Summary
At BMS, digital innovation and Information Technology are central to our vision of transforming patients' lives through science. To accelerate our ability to serve patients around the world, we must unleash the power of technology. We are committed to being at the forefront of transforming the way medicine is made and delivered by harnessing the power of computer and data science, artificial intelligence, and other technologies to promote scientific discovery, faster decision making, and enhanced patient care.

The Product Owner, Workforce Planning (People Technology) will co-own the product vision, roadmap, and backlog for BMS's Workforce Planning capability, built on Workday Adaptive Planning and integrated with Workday HCM — while also hands-on building and maintaining the Adaptive Planning integrations, security/permissions, reports, and dashboards that power it. Having established the foundational platform, this role will drive the next phase of the journey: maturing workforce planning from headcount and budget forecasting toward strategic workforce planning — including scenario-based org design, skills and talent supply/demand analysis, and long-range workforce modeling that directly informs business and talent strategy.
This role partners closely with the business Product Manager, People Organization, and Finance leaders to translate evolving workforce planning needs into a prioritized backlog, and personally builds and maintains the integrations, security, reports, and dashboards that keep the platform accurate, secure, and trusted as the capability matures.
If you want an exciting and rewarding career that is meaningful, consider joining our team!

Key Responsibilities
Workforce Planning Product Strategy
- Co-own, with the business Product Manager, the vision and multi-year roadmap for Strategic Workforce Planning, evolving the capability beyond current-state headcount/budget planning toward scenario planning, org design modeling, and skills/talent-based forecasting.
- Translate People Organization and Finance strategy into workforce planning requirements — e.g., how the business plans headcount, org structure changes, span of control, succession, and talent pipelines — and prioritize these in the Adaptive Planning backlog.
- Identify and prioritize opportunities to mature the model (new dimensions, planning versions, scenario types) as the business's workforce planning maturity increases.

Hands-On Build: Integrations, Security, Reports & Dashboards
- Design, build, and maintain integrations between Workday HCM and Adaptive Planning, ensuring accurate, timely data flows for headcount, compensation, organizational dimensions, and planning versions.
- Configure and maintain Adaptive Planning security and permissions — roles, level and version access, and security groups — ensuring the right stakeholders can plan, model, and report at the right level of the organization, and that sensitive workforce data is properly protected.
- Build and maintain reports and dashboards (e.g., Adaptive Discovery Boards, OfficeConnect, Workday reporting) that give HR, Finance, and business leaders visibility into workforce plans, scenarios, and variances.
- Troubleshoot and resolve data quality, integration, security, and calculation issues directly, partnering with Workday HCM and Adaptive Planning admins as needed.
- Continuously enhance existing integrations, security configurations, reports, and dashboards based on stakeholder feedback and evolving workforce planning maturity.

Adaptive Planning Model Design
- Own the backlog and hands-on build for Adaptive Planning models (sheets, dimensions, attributes, versions, assumptions) that represent the organization's workforce structure, positions, and headcount plans.
- Coordinate with stakeholders on cross-system interfaces (e.g., payroll, benefits, time & attendance) that feed or influence workforce planning assumptions, ensuring upstream/downstream data quality.

Governance, Testing & Enablement
- Co-own governance and change control for the workforce planning product — model updates, assumptions, planning calendars, security changes, and integration schedules — aligning with enterprise SDLC and release processes.
- Own and execute testing and deployment (unit, system, UAT, regression) for integrations, security/permission changes, models, reports, and dashboards; ensure planning cycles (budget, forecast, headcount reviews) are supported without disruption.
- Drive stakeholder training and enablement for People Organization business partners, Finance, and leadership — model walkthroughs, scenario planning usage, and report/dashboard usage — to build organizational fluency as capabilities mature.
- Monitor adoption, performance, and data quality metrics to identify where the platform and process need to evolve next.

Platform Currency & Innovation
- Stay current on Workday releases relevant to Adaptive Planning and HCM (planning features, security, integration enhancements, AI/ML-driven workforce insights) and assess fit against the strategic workforce planning roadmap.
- Champion best practices in workforce analytics and planning automation; partner with People Organization, Finance, and People Analytics teams to pilot innovations (e.g., skills taxonomy integration, predictive attrition/demand modeling) that move the capability toward strategic workforce planning.
- Provide leadership and guidance to cross-functional team members supporting the product, ensuring engagement and productivity.

Qualifications & Experience
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Human Resources, Finance, or a related discipline.
- 5+ years of experience in HR or Finance technology, with strong exposure to workforce planning, Workday Adaptive Planning , and Workday HCM; product ownership or business analysis experience preferred.
- Hands-on, demonstrated expertise building and maintaining Workday Adaptive Planning integrations, models (sheets, dimensions, versions, assumptions), and security/permissions configuration (roles, level and version access, security groups).

Roadmap Execution & Product Delivery

Data Governance

Data Modeling & Domain Design

- Support design and implementation of logical and physical data models.
- Contribute to commercial domain definitions and maintain version-controlled model documentation following governance review processes.

Data Catalog Management

- Support build-out and adoption of the enterprise data catalog ensuring datasets are catalogued with accurate metadata, lineage, and ownership.

Data Quality & Operational Excellence

Adoption, Vendor & Budget Support

- Support vendor management, SLA monitoring, budget tracking, and research of new technology and tooling options.

- Demonstrated ability to lead delivery and execution through strong stakeholder engagement and cross‑functional collaboration (Commercial, Analytics, IT, Compliance, vendors).

- Working knowledge of modern data platforms and lakehouse architectures (e.g., Databricks) and how curated data products are delivered and consumed.
- Strong understanding of operational data governance, including ownership, definitions, classification, approved usage, and privacy/retention controls.
- Experience implementing and monitoring data quality controls and coordinating issue resolution across data pipelines and vendors.
- Familiarity with metadata and data cataloging to support discoverability, certification, and governed self‑service access.
- Exposure to third‑party commercial data and operationalization of licensing, redistribution, and retention constraints.
- Understanding of the regulatory and compliance landscape governing Medical Affairs data (e.g., PhRMA Code, off-label inquiry handling, HCP transparency/Sunshine Act reporting) and how it shapes data access, classification, and usage controls.

Position Summary:
Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) is seeking an exceptional leader for the position of Executive Director, Product Development, Analytical Services & Direct Material, within PDS Procurement. The role brings Product Development, Analytical Services and Direct Materials Procurement together under a single leader, spanning market-facing spend of approximately $1B across the end-to-end product lifecycle, from early development through commercial manufacturing.
PDS Procurement is a corporate strategic sourcing group dedicated to supporting the company's global business units by developing and implementing innovative sourcing strategies. Our mission is to maximize contract value while maintaining the highest quality standards through clear specifications and well-planned negotiations. The team continuously collaborates with strategic suppliers to enhance and capture additional value within the supply chain through productivity initiatives and strong partnerships.
As the Executive Director, you will lead the integration of Direct Materials Procurement into the existing Product Development & Analytical Services organization, harmonizing category strategies, governance, and ways of working across Product Development, Analytical Services, and Direct Materials. You will ensure delivery of category value targets, as agreed with finance and business stakeholders and endorsed by the PDS Procurement Leadership Team (SLT), and will be expected to be a credible leader and value-adding business partner to senior stakeholders at the VP and Senior VP levels.
In collaboration with the SLT and business stakeholders, the Executive Director will lead the development, implementation, and maintenance of formalized category management structures and methods across all three sub-categories. This includes ensuring effective supplier relationship management, including with small business suppliers, to drive performance delivery, continuous improvement, and access to innovation. By applying rigorous category management tools, systems, and techniques, the Executive Director will deliver measurable business value, both operational and financial, while ensuring the combined team operates as a single, cohesive function.
Additionally, you will take personal ownership of the largest and/or most complex supplier arrangements across the combined portfolio and provide subject matter expertise to your extended team on other supply and commercial conditions.
Competencies/Skills:
- Global Procurement Leadership Across Development & Direct Materials: Proven track record leading procurement for Product Development, Analytical Services/Quality, and/or Direct Materials categories within the biopharmaceutical, pharmaceutical, or medical device industry, and demonstrated ability to work successfully with international colleagues in a highly collaborative manner and culture.

- Organizational Design & Change Leadership: Demonstrated experience integrating a new category or team into an established organization, and leading organizations through significant structural change.

- Exceptional Communication and Presentation Skills: Ability to communicate effectively across multiple levels within the company, with demonstrated capability to influence decision-making processes both through virtual and in-person audiences.

- Strong Problem-Solving Skills: Adept at working cross-functionally as a critical member of the Procurement leadership team and across other Global Procurement Towers.

- Leadership in Project Management: Experience leading projects and initiatives with significant global and site impact, achieving milestones and objectives using the category management lifecycle.

- Business Acumen and Strategic Thinking: Ability to manage business complexities and develop sustainable solutions, providing a clear roadmap for success across multiple, distinct spend categories.

- Business Partnering Orientation: Strong analytic, interpersonal, communication, and negotiation skills, with a focus on building and maintaining effective business partnerships.

- Proactive and Innovative Approach: Creative and analytical mindset for continuous improvement in procurement services and identifying new opportunities.

- Independence and Self-Motivation: Demonstrated high degree of independence, requiring minimal supervision from senior management.

- Technical Proficiency: Knowledge and proficiency with procurement systems such as Ariba is preferred.

- Industry Certifications: Relevant industry certifications (e.g., CPM, CPSM, CSCP, CPIM) are preferred.

- Change Management: Experience in leading and managing change within a complex organizational environment through process re-engineering and evaluation/implementation of best practices and leading technologies.

- Global Market Insight: Deep understanding of global market trends across development, analytical services, and direct materials supply chains and their impact on procurement strategies.

- Risk Management: Expertise in identifying and mitigating supply continuity, quality, and commercial risks associated with procurement activities.

- Sustainability Focus: Commitment to sustainable procurement practices and corporate social responsibility.

- Innovation Mindset: Ability to incorporate newest technologies as part of the category strategy.

- Customer Service Mindset: Ability to lead through influence rather than authority.

Responsibilities include:
Organizational Leadership & Team Integration
- Lead the integration of Direct Materials Procurement into the existing, combined Product Development & Analytical Services organization, extending established governance and reporting standards to the newly added category.

- Establish common governance, category management routines, and reporting standards across the three combined sub-functions.

- Identify and capture synergies across the combined team, including shared supplier relationships, tools, and processes where appropriate.

- Lead change management activities to build a single, cohesive team culture and minimize disruption to business partners as Direct Materials joins the team.

Strategic Sourcing and Category Management
- Develop and implement a cohesive, long-term (3-5 year) category strategy for each sub-category, consolidating supplier, market, category, and internal business data.

- Lead the aggregation of category data to inform target setting, identifying initiatives and opportunities for savings, productivity, risk management, and innovation.

- Create and oversee the Annual Category Plan for the combined portfolio, ensuring alignment with business planning activities and category pipeline to meet or exceed annual targets.

- Develop and maintain a category management handbook to provide clear, practical guidance for procurement and functional colleagues.

- Lead and coach cross-functional global teams through category management stages, ensuring resources, information, and tools are in place for project execution.

- Ensure accurate reporting of procurement balanced scorecard measures and value contributions for each category.

- Implement programs to deliver spend accuracy in line with agreed goals.

- Conduct regular risk and CSR reviews within the combined category scope.

Supplier Performance and Risk Management
- Perform supplier segmentation across Product Development, Analytical Services, and Direct Materials to identify key relationships and conduct regular business reviews to ensure delivery to expectations and target value.

- Establish value creation targets with key suppliers in partnership with business stakeholders.

- Ensure contractual arrangements incorporate compliance and performance against KPIs.

- Assess and mitigate risks associated with supplier relationships and supply chain disruptions, including single-source and quality-critical materials.

Cost Management and Savings
- Drive cost reduction and optimization initiatives and identify savings opportunities across development, analytical, and direct materials categories.

- Develop and monitor budgets, ensuring alignment with financial goals and objectives.

- Negotiate contracts and agreements to secure favorable terms and conditions based on fair market values.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
- Work closely with R&D, Quality, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain stakeholders to understand needs and requirements across all three sub-categories.

- Collaborate with global procurement teams to ensure alignment and consistency in sourcing strategies.

- Facilitate communication and coordination between internal stakeholders and suppliers.

- Develop strong working relationships with key business stakeholders and administrative functions (Finance, HR, Legal, Privacy, Compliance).

Governance and Compliance
- Ensure adherence to company policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements, including GMP where applicable.

- Develop and maintain procurement governance frameworks to support decision-making and accountability across the combined team.

- Monitor and report on compliance with contractual obligations and performance metrics.

Leadership and Team Development
- Lead and mentor a team of procurement professionals across Product Development, Analytical Services, and Direct Materials, fostering a culture of continuous improvement and excellence.

- Provide guidance and support to team members, helping them achieve professional goals through individual development plans.

- Promote a collaborative and inclusive work environment.

- Establish clear roles and responsibilities for the extended category team and communicate them effectively.

- Conduct performance management for direct reports and provide feedback for project-related resources.

- Develop a succession plan to support career development and ensure a talent pipeline.

Innovation and Continuous Improvement
- Identify and implement innovative procurement practices and technologies to enhance efficiency and effectiveness.

- Drive continuous improvement initiatives to optimize procurement processes and performance across the combined team.

- Stay informed of industry advancements and emerging trends to maintain a competitive edge.

Stakeholder Engagement and Communication
- Build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, both internal and external.

- Communicate procurement strategies, initiatives, and performance to senior leadership and other stakeholders.

- Act as a trusted advisor to the business, providing insights and recommendations on procurement-related matters.

Education:
- B.S./B.A. required; M.S./M.B.A. preferred.

Experience:
- Minimum 15 years of international business experience, with 10-12 years in multi-disciplined procurement, ideally spanning two or more of: Product Development, Analytical Services/Quality, or Direct Materials (sourcing or otherwise).

- Extensive knowledge of category management and advanced strategic sourcing methodologies.

- Demonstrated success leading global cross-functional project teams to generate material value across multiple, distinct complex categories.

- Documented experience leading cost reduction and value improvement programs.

- Proven experience leading large-scale organizational change and/or team integration efforts.

- Management experience, including prior experience in the biopharmaceutical, pharmaceutical, and/or medical device industry.

- Demonstrated successful leadership track record, including managing teams of senior professionals and managers, and establishing performance expectations.

- Experience in GMP procurement required.

Travel Requirements:
- High flexibility and willingness to travel (air, ground; both domestic and international) for various meetings at BMS and supplier sites.

Onsite Requirements:
- 50% over a 2-week span on-site attendance requirement.
